newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU pigmeat production seen 1.5 pct higher in 1997.
newsitem.headline: EU pigmeat production seen 1.5 pct higher in 1997.

text.p: Pigmeat production in the European Union may rise by 1.5 percent to 16.5 million tonnes in 1997, the Bonn farm ministry said in a circular, citing information from the EU statistics office, Eurostat.

It said some 143 million animals would come up for slaughter in the Januar-September period, some two million or 1.4 percent more than in comparable 1996, not counting mandatory slaughterings after an outbreak of swine fever.
The ministry said German pigmeat prices would ease because of lower exports into third countries but profitability would remain satisfactory.
Germany leads the group of EU producer countries with a forecast 27.6 million slaughterings in January-September, after 27.2 million in the same 1996 period.
Slaughterings during the nine months in Spain should be 20.5 million (20.4), followed by 18.8 million in France (18.4), the Netherlands with 17.8 (17.9) and Denmark with 15.5 (15.2).

The last EU animal count in December 1996 showed 118 million pigs, two million more than a year earlier, of which Germany accounted for 24.1 million (23.7), followed by Spain's 18.5 (18.1) and France's 15.0 (14.5).
